reason: The active panel32 reduction loop loads both operands, advances both pointers, then updates all four ZA tiles. Moving the pointer adds between FMOPA operations is a small, bounded schedule change that preserves each tile’s FP32 order. The proposed load lookahead also targets this active loop, but needs careful prologue and drain bounds. SUBS/B.NE is low risk, though it still uses two instructions. Packing B per panel and fusing transpose with consumption may reduce data movement, but add layout, allocation, or assembly complexity. Prefetch and A-slice padding have weaker support: the prior prefetch result was on the inactive path, and the supplied evidence does not establish cache conflicts. Smaller scratch adds K-block loop work; the 1 MiB B layout and fallback-only transpose change have the largest timed-cost or relevance concerns. No proposal has measured evidence of a gain on the active path.
